functionalReqs: Pay-in: charge a customer for an order via a PSP (cards, UPI, wallets)
Payment status queryable by the order service
hints: The PSP call timed out. Did the charge happen? What lets you retry safely?
Use idempotency keys end-to-end and a double-entry ledger as the source of truth.

Payment service with a state machine (created → pending → succeeded/failed), idempotency key per order, PSP-hosted payment page (avoid storing cards), webhooks plus polling for status, double-entry ledger, wallet balances, daily reconciliation against PSP settlement files, and retries with a dead-letter queue.
nonFunctionalReqs: Correctness above all: no double charges, no lost money
Highly available; slow PSPs are tolerated
problemStatement:
Design the **payment backend** for an e-commerce company: it charges customers through payment service providers (PSPs) and pays out to sellers.

Money must never be charged twice or lost, even when networks time out mid-request.
